text_blocks.snippet: In radiation treatment, the standard measure of energy deposited in tissue is the gray (Gy), which represents the amount of energy (joules) absorbed per kilogram of tissue. It's the international (SI) unit for absorbed dose. Historically, the rad was used, but it has been largely replaced by the gray (1 Gy = 100 rad).

list.title: Absorbed Dose:
list.snippet: Radiation treatment aims to deliver a specific amount of energy to a tumor or targeted area while minimizing damage to surrounding healthy tissue. The absorbed dose quantifies this energy deposition.

list.title: Gray (Gy):
list.snippet: The gray is defined as one joule of energy absorbed per kilogram of tissue (1 Gy = 1 J/kg).

list.title: Centigray (cGy):
list.snippet: In clinical settings, you might also encounter the centigray (cGy), which is one hundredth of a gray (1 cGy = 0.01 Gy).

list.title: Historical Context:
list.snippet: The rad (radiation absorbed dose) was the earlier unit for absorbed dose, but the gray has become the standard, though the rad is still sometimes used, particularly in the US.
